name: GM Arnold Denker National Tournament of High School State Champions
value: Published 2026 scholarships: $5,000, $4,000, $3,000, $2,000 and $1,000 for ranks 1 to 5; cash $800, $500, $400, $300 and $200, split for ties. Scholarship claims require at least half-time higher-education enrollment and must be made before age 26. Other 2026 awards include $1,000 Ursula Foster, $100 under-2000 Joanne Haskel and $100 biggest overall upset. The 2027 prize schedule is not published.
deadline: The national page still lists the completed August 3 to 6, 2026 event and June 1, 2026 state nominations. A 2027 state event listing places the related U.S. Open in Dallas August 2 to 8, 2027, but the exact 2027 Denker dates and nomination cutoff are not published on the national rules page. State selection deadlines vary.
apply: Earn your state affiliate's nomination using its chosen qualification method. Under published 2026 rules, the affiliate submits the nomination, the player separately confirms participation promptly, and onsite check-in/opening ceremony and all six rounds are required. The 2027 national confirmation timetable is not published.
eligibility: Published 2026 rules: state-approved grades 9 to 12 curriculum at qualification, state residency at that stage, current US Chess membership during Denker, and age 19 or younger on September 1 of the event year. Dual enrollment is allowed. D.C. counts as a state and California has separate north/south representatives. A player may represent only one state and play only one simultaneous national invitational. Complete 2027 rules are not published.
notes: National entry is free; players pay their travel and accommodations. Scholarship ties use tiebreak scores, while cash ties are split. Ursula Foster normally goes to the top finisher age 15 or younger, with an age-16 fallback if fewer than two age-15 entrants compete. Cash payments of $2,000 or more require a W-9. Extra U.S. Junior/World Youth qualification has separate eligibility, including a U.S. FIDE flag.

name: USA Brain Bee National Championship
value: 2026 cash prizes: first $1,500, second $1,000 and third $500; the national winner advances to the International Brain Bee. The next-cycle prize/fee and travel arrangements are not published.
deadline: 2027 national and local qualifying dates are not posted. The national page still lists the completed April 25, 2026 UC Irvine championship; local chapter deadlines vary.
apply: Win one local chapter Brain Bee, then receive the national registration link and have eligibility confirmed with the chapter. The 2026 national registration fee was $400, including event participation/meals for the competitor and one chaperone; extra guest meals cost $50. New-cycle registration and fees are not published.
eligibility: Published rules: age 13 to 19 at competition and current or former enrollment in an accredited U.S. high school. Only one local chapter competition per year; only one national championship and one International World Championship in a lifetime. A local chapter victory is required nationally. Complete 2027 cycle terms are not posted.
notes: The 2026 fee does not cover hotel/airfare; a hotel group rate and shuttle were offered. Competition includes neuroscience questions, anatomy/histology/MRI identification and clinical/scientific reasoning. Unauthorized notes/devices, plagiarism or outside help lead to dismissal.

name: Stulberg International String Competition
value: 2027 Gold $10,000, Silver $7,000 and Bronze $5,000, each with an orchestra performance award; medal prize money is paid half after competition and half after the performance award concert. Bach Prize $2,000; the other nine semifinalists receive $1,000 each.
deadline: Opens October 19, 2026; complete application February 1, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. EST. Results by March 15, 2027. Live semifinals May 14, 2027, finals May 15, 2027 and required semifinalist masterclasses May 16, 2027 in Kalamazoo, Michigan.
apply: Submit through Acceptd with a nonrefundable $150 credit-card fee and one unedited video, at most 20 minutes, of one eligible solo work originally written for your instrument and orchestra. Perform from memory with live piano/orchestra accompaniment; no digital accompaniment or identifying names/school/teacher on the video. Recording must be from February 1, 2026 or later. If selected, keep the audition repertoire for live semifinals and prepare the required solo Bach selection.
eligibility: Violinists, violists, cellists and double bassists age 19 or under as of January 1, 2027. Current students of the 2027 judges are ineligible.
notes: The full current 2027 application guidelines are published. Twelve semifinalists and four ranked alternates are selected; six advance to finals. Medalists have later concerto performance commitments, which determine payment of the second half of the cash award.

name: FBA Civics Essay Contest
value: Published scholarship prizes: first $1,500, second $1,250, third $750. The closed-cycle FAQ describes these as prior prizes; the 2027 prize/payment terms are not published.
deadline: The 2026 contest is closed. FBA says the new prompt will be posted in January 2027; the 2027 entry deadline is not published.
apply: When the contest opens, submit the annual-prompt essay and completed official entry form online. Published rules require a Word document, maximum 1,000 words excluding endnotes/bibliography, double spacing, 12-point Cambria or Times New Roman, one-inch margins and a student-name filename. The 2027 prompt and entry form are not posted.
eligibility: Grades 9 to 12 at public, private, parochial or charter schools, or homeschool equivalent, in the United States and territories. Prior winners may re-enter until graduating.
notes: Judged on constitutional understanding, clarity/theme, grammar/composition and citations. Extensive AI drafting, plagiarism, off-topic or improperly formatted essays can disqualify an entry. FBA retains publishing rights and may copyright/reprint submitted material. The 2027 prompt will be released in January; no finalist announcements are planned under the current FAQ.

name: Regions Riding Forward Scholarship Contest
value: Each of four 2026 quarterly contests awards four $8,000 college scholarships, two written-essay and two video-essay winners. Paid to the designated accredited nonprofit U.S. undergraduate college; use fully by the end of 2027-28 for tuition/books/room/board or other college expenses. Unused funds may be forfeited; no graduate-school use.
deadline: 2026 Q3 closes September 30, 2026; Q4 opens October 1, 2026 and closes December 31, 2026, both at 11:59:59 p.m. Central Time. Approximate Q3 winners November 30, 2026; Q4 winners February 28, 2027. Potential winners respond and submit required documents within 10 business days; identify the college within 30 days after award notification/acceptance.
apply: Complete the online quarterly application using program key RidingForward and submit one English written essay of at most 500 words OR an English video of at most three minutes about a personally known community member who inspired you. Minors need guardian electronic consent, including Mississippi residents under 21. Video must show only you, contain no music or third-party logos, and be an accepted format up to 1 GB. Winners supply a notarized affidavit/release/copyright assignment, current transcript and photo.
eligibility: Legal U.S. residents of AL, AR, FL, GA, IA, IL, IN, KY, LA, MS, MO, NC, SC, TN or TX, age at least 16, with at least one year or 18 semester hours before undergraduate graduation. Students not yet in college must start by 2027-28. Cumulative school GPA at least 2.0, or good standing/equivalent if the school gives no GPA. No Regions account or purchase required. One entry per quarter and one win in the entire 2026 contest.
notes: Independent judges score inspiration 50%, originality/creativity 25% and quality 25%; no vote or random drawing. Work must be original, unpublished, not previously awarded or entered in another competition, and created without AI. Regions receives broad usage rights; winners may need the subject's publicity release and an eligibility/background check. These verified rules are for the remaining 2026 quarterly contests and expressly allow college entry in 2027-28.

name: OG&E Positive Energy Scholarship
value: Three $15,000 annual scholarships, up to $60,000 over four years, for tuition, books, fees and on-campus room/board. The 2026 announcement required at least 2.75 unweighted GPA for renewal and continued approved-major study; complete 2027 renewal terms are not published.
deadline: Applications are closed and the sponsor says they will reopen in fall 2026. The 2027 deadline is not published; January 15, 2026 was the prior cycle closing date.
apply: Use the application linked by OG&E/Oklahoma City Community Foundation when it reopens. The current directory confirms the scholarship, but full next-cycle required application materials are not publicly available.
eligibility: High school seniors whose primary residence is in the OG&E service area in Oklahoma/western Arkansas, attending college in Oklahoma or Arkansas in an OG&E-designated STEM-related major. The sponsor says recipients are OG&E customers. The current administrator directory confirms a 3.25 GPA minimum; the 2026 press release specified unweighted GPA and included business among approved majors. Complete 2027 rules are not published.
notes: The current scholarship directory independently confirms the 3.25 GPA, service-area and college/major requirements. The full 2026 approved-major list contains more than the previously stated 23 majors, so use the actual current list when the next application opens. Renewal, application materials and next deadline remain unpublished for 2027.

name: Alliant Energy Innovation Scholarship
value: Published annual program: up to 25 one-year undergraduate awards of $1,000, not renewable. The administrator's 2026 guidance describes one June payment; a 2027 payment date is not published.
deadline: Sponsor lists an annual December 2 to February 3 window without years. The administrator is closed and still refers to the 2026 program; exact 2027 dates are not confirmed.
apply: Apply through Scholarship America with a current complete transcript, including name, school, grades, credits and terms, and a 350-word essay. Grade reports are not accepted. The full upcoming portal is not open.
eligibility: Current sponsor guidelines: high school senior with community-service/volunteer leadership, U.S. residence in Alliant's service territory, age 24 or under, and applicant or dependent-child relationship to a utility customer in good standing. Enroll for the first time full time in STEM or a skilled trade at an accredited Iowa/Wisconsin school within Alliant's service territory, with GPA 2.5 to 4.0 on a 4.0 scale or equivalent. High-school dual enrollment is allowed. Company/administrator employees and specified family/household members are excluded.
notes: Financial need is not considered. The current sponsor independently publishes the GPA, first-time study, leadership and customer requirements; the administrator still labels its 2026 information tentative. Student customers are eligible in their own right, so applicants need not all be dependent children.

name: Edison Scholars Program
value: 30 scholarships of $50,000 over four years. Published administrator terms provide $12,500 per year and renewal up to three more years or a bachelor's degree, with satisfactory academics, full-time approved-major study and program continuation. Military-academy recipients receive a one-time nonrenewable award. These detailed terms are still labeled 2026/tentative; final 2027 terms are unpublished.
deadline: The sponsor says the 2027 program opens in fall 2026 but gives no exact dates. The prior application closed January 22, 2026; its recommendation deadline was February 6, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. CST. These are not 2027 deadlines.
apply: Sign up for 2027 opening updates. Published 2026 administrator requirements include complete transcript, two 1,000-character written responses, one nonrelative online recommendation, first two pages of family IRS 1040 with identifiers redacted, headshot and SCE customer/account number from a family utility bill. Top 50 finalists submit a video at most two minutes; 2027 full materials are not yet posted.
eligibility: Current sponsor independently requires high school senior status, at least 3.0 cumulative GPA, financial need, SCE-service-area residence and an accredited four-year STEM programme; employee/retiree dependents are excluded. Prior administrator guidance also required an SCE family utility-account number and full-time U.S. study for 2026-27; complete 2027 administrator criteria are unpublished.
notes: Eligible fields include computing/information systems, engineering/engineering technology, mathematics, natural resources/conservation and physical sciences. Scholars may apply for a paid SCE internship after the first college year, subject to eligibility and hiring screening; the internship is not guaranteed. Current sponsor GPA/geography criteria are independent of the old-cycle administrator guide.

name: Dominion Energy Educational Equity Scholarship Program
value: Published amounts: $5,000 for two-year programs and $10,000 for four-year degrees; renewable up to three additional years or a bachelor's degree. Full-time enrollment, continued eligible-state residence and program continuation are required. Sponsor says renewal GPA 2.5; administrator says 2.0. Final 2027 award/renewal rules are not posted.
deadline: 2027 dates are not posted. The sponsor lists March 12 at 4 p.m. Eastern/3 p.m. Central without a year; the administrator is closed and still labels information as tentative for 2026. Its recommendation is due within three business days after the application deadline under the displayed rules.
apply: Apply through Scholarship America when the next cycle opens. Published materials include a current complete transcript, first two pages of the most recent IRS 1040 with Social Security numbers redacted, one online recommendation and requested goals/community information. Supply a separate SAT/ACT report only if providing scores not shown on a high-school transcript. The full 2027 application is not published.
eligibility: High school seniors, graduates or current undergraduates in CT, MD, NC, SC, VA or WV, planning full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-/four-year college or vocational-technical school. The sponsor lists a 3.0 GPA minimum; the administrator's current eligibility list does not state a minimum and adds commitment to a welcoming community. Exact 2027 eligibility should be confirmed when the application opens.
notes: 80% of awards combine financial need and merit; 20% are merit only. The sponsor expressly states awards are without regard to race, ethnicity, religion, gender and other listed characteristics. Current official pages disagree on the renewal GPA and notification month, and final 2027 terms are not published.

name: Unitil STEM Scholarships
value: Five public scholarships of $5,000 each for the first year of undergraduate STEM study. In 2026 a sixth award went to an employee's child; that separate award is not a general public slot.
deadline: 2027-28 cycle not yet posted; the 2026-2027 application has closed.
apply: Use the online application portal when open. Current guidelines require an official high-school transcript, recommendation from a STEM teacher or principal verifying the major and expected graduation, and an essay on career objectives, reasons for applying and merit.
eligibility: High school seniors who live in and attend school in eligible Unitil service-territory towns in New Hampshire, Massachusetts and Maine and who declare a STEM major.
notes: Recipients are selected on academic merit, financial need, other awards, activities and work hours. Both primary residence and school must be in eligible Unitil service-territory towns. The current page reports 2026 awards and says the 2026-27 application is closed; the next-cycle dates are unpublished.

name: Robert E. Evans Scholarship
value: Award amounts vary by available funding and recipient count. The 2027-28 individual amount, payment duration and renewal conditions are not published.
deadline: 2027-28 application opens January 4, 2027. The FAQ gives a recurring March 31 closing date, while the explicitly dated prior deadline was March 31, 2026; the page has not explicitly confirmed the 2027 closing date.
apply: Apply online after January 4, 2027. Financial need must be documented using the FAFSA Student Aid Report requested by the official page; the complete next-cycle application and additional materials are not published.
eligibility: High school seniors living within a Peoples Bank market/service area in Ohio, Kentucky, West Virginia, Virginia, Maryland or Washington, D.C., with at least 3.5 GPA and financial need. Plan an accredited four-year degree in business, education, engineering, liberal arts, mathematics, science or technology. State residence alone does not establish service-area eligibility.
notes: Need is required, with preference for higher need. The current page explicitly confirms the January 4, 2027 opening and current general GPA/market-area rules, but does not provide the individual 2027-28 award amount or complete application/payment terms.

name: Rotary Club of Los Angeles Scholarships
value: Published 2026 award: $10,000 paid directly to each scholar in four annual $2,500 installments. Later installments require continued enrollment, a minimum GPA not specified on the public page, and 10 hours of community service. The 2026 portal planned 20 awards; 2027 award count and renewal terms are not published.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was March 2, 2026.
apply: Apply through the official Kaleidoscope portal when the next cycle opens. The club evaluates applicants and conducts interviews. A blank application link is present but its content is not publicly readable, and complete 2027 materials are not published.
eligibility: College-bound high school seniors graduating from schools in Los Angeles County, entering a four-year college/university in fall, with academic excellence and strong community service. The portal currently describes the 2026 cycle; final 2027 rules are unpublished.
notes: Prioritizes high-need, high-performing students. Typical recipient GPAs of 3.7 to 4.0 unweighted are descriptive, not a stated initial minimum. The club page's 25-award statement is tied to 2021; the 2026 application planned 20 awards.

name: Rotary Four-Way Test Speech Contest (District 7390)
value: District finals: $1,250 (1st), $750 (2nd), $500 (3rd), $250 each (4th and 5th)
deadline: 2026-27 cycle: club winners must be submitted by March 13, 2027; mid-level round March 27, 2027; finals April 17, 2027.
apply: Enter one local Rotary club contest and submit the contestant entry form before participating. The club representative enters its winner by March 13, 2027; only one student per school district may advance, with a runner-up substitution if needed. Attend the March 27, 2027 mid-level contest in Enola and, if selected among its top five, the April 17, 2027 finals in Reading. Local club entry deadlines vary.
eligibility: Grades 10 to 12 at a public, private or charter high school or homeschool within District 7390, and resident of Adams, Cumberland, Dauphin, Lancaster, Lebanon, Perry or York County, PA. Only one club contest per student per year.
notes: Original speech on a chosen topic, applying all four principles throughout. Length 5 to 8 minutes, with two-point penalties per 15 seconds or fraction outside the range. Notes allowed at club level; one non-electronic 3 x 5 card at mid-level; no notes at finals. No props at mid-level or finals. Both advancing rounds require in-person attendance.

name: High School Student Four-Way Test Speech Contest (District 5930)
value: Published 2026 district prizes: $1,500 first, $1,000 second, $750 third, and $100 to other district contestants, paid directly or mailed. Club/area awards vary. Final 2027 amounts are not published.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; in 2026 club contests were due March 14, area contests March 25, and the District Championship was April 11, 2026.
apply: Compete at a local Rotary club, with first- and second-place winners advancing to area and then district. The published 2026 consent form requires original work not used in UIL or another non-Rotary competition, student signature and parent/guardian signature for ages 17 or younger. Photo/speech publication consent can be declined on that form. Final 2027 forms are not published.
eligibility: Published rules welcome high school students in District 5930, South Texas. Prior district first-place winners cannot compete again at district level. Multiple club contests are permitted if allowed by the clubs. Exact 2027 rules are not yet published.
notes: Published rules require a 5 to 7 minute speech relating the Four-Way Test to the student's experiences; speeches outside the range are disqualified. Content counts 50%, organization 30%, delivery 20%; note cards are allowed. Do not identify school or club until after judging. Published 2026 rules arrange transportation/lodging through area coordinators and sponsoring clubs, with lunch for the contestant and one guest.

provider: Rotary District 5340 (San Diego and Imperial Valley)
name: Rotary Four-Way Test Speech Contest (District 5340)
value: District finals: $1,000 grand prize, $750 runner-up, $500 other finalists; awards also at club, subregional and regional levels
deadline: 2026-27 cycle: local club contests take place in January and February 2027, followed by subregional/regional rounds. District finals are April 22, 2027. Individual club entry deadlines vary.
apply: Be selected with teacher help and sponsored by a District 5340 Rotary club; advance through club, subregional and regional contests. Complete the district photo-release form, with parent signature if under 18. The district says updated resources will be available at fourwaytest-5340.org starting October 10, 2026.
eligibility: High school students ages 14 to 18 residing in Rotary District 5340 (San Diego and Imperial Valley) who have not previously won first place.
notes: Original 5 to 7 minute speech applying the Four-Way Test; no props, with penalties outside the time range. Notes allowed at club/subregional level without reading the whole speech; one 3 x 5 card at regionals and no notes at finals.

name: Rotary 4-Way Test Speech Contest (District 5790)
value: Club, regional and district cash awards vary by year and budget. Final 2027 prize amounts are not posted.
deadline: 2026-27 cycle: regionals April 3, April 10 and April 17, 2027, at locations to be announced. District final April 24, 2027 at District Assembly. Local club entry/contest deadlines vary.
apply: Compete through a sponsoring Rotary club; each club sends one winner (or runner-up substitute) through regionals to the district final. The club submits the student application and photo/video consent, with parent/guardian signature for students under 18. Linked forms are still labeled 2025-26; a complete updated 2026-27 form is not posted.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9 to 12 (homeschoolers welcome) in the North Texas area of District 5790 who have not competed at the district level in a prior year.
notes: Current page specifies What the Four-Way Test Means to Me, original work, five-minute limit with 30-second grace period, no written scripts or props, and permitted 3 x 5 note cards. Prior district-level contestants are ineligible. Interact membership is not required. The linked 2025-26 rules assess a 5% penalty after 5 minutes 30 seconds; updated linked documents are not yet posted.

name: William J. Schulz Memorial Essay Contest for College-Bound High School Seniors
value: First through tenth place awards from $3,500 down to $300, plus optional honorable mentions of $200 each (2026 contest)
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was June 1, 2026.
apply: Use the official online essay application when the next contest opens. The published 2026 prompt required a 350 to 500 word personal essay about a freethought/humanist hero, documenting nonreligious views and quotations/facts with links or footnotes. The complete 2027 prompt, form and rules are not published.
eligibility: Published 2026 rules cover high school seniors graduating in spring/summer and entering college in fall, including gap-year graduates entering college in fall 2026. Only one FFRF contest per year, and no re-entry in a contest where the student previously won an award. Final 2027 criteria are not published.
notes: The 2026 prompt asks students to explain their chosen person's influence and what that person means to them as a humanist/nonbeliever. Published prior rules barred AI-generated writing beyond grammar/spellcheck; the complete next-cycle rules are not available.

name: Bennington Young Creators Awards (Young Artists, Innovators, Musicians and Scientists)
value: Cash prizes in each discipline: First $2,000, Second $1,000, Third $500, Distinguished $250. If enrolling at Bennington: First Place full tuition for four years, Distinguished half tuition for four years, Finalists $25,000 per year for four years.
deadline: 2026-27 cycle: opens September 1, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Eastern; closes November 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. Winners announced in spring 2027.
apply: Submit one entry per discipline, choosing one category within it, with sponsoring teacher/mentor review and approval. Grades 9 to 11 use the YCA registration/portal; grade 12 first submits a nonbinding Common or Coalition Application to Bennington, then receives YCA instructions. Artists: one 2D image, up to three 3D images, or 1 to 2 minute digital work; optional description up to 500 words. Musicians: one original composition up to five minutes; recording/MIDI strongly recommended, optional score/lyrics, English translation for other-language lyrics. Scientists: a natural-science visual artifact, up to five PDF/images, optional explanation up to 500 words. Innovators: AI creative work plus 500 to 750 word reflection, a critical essay up to 1,200 words plus AI-use note up to 300 words if applicable, or a practical AI project with video up to three minutes and explanation up to 500 words.
eligibility: Students in grades 9 to 12 worldwide; graduated students are not eligible.
notes: Free entry; a student may win in only one discipline. This listing covers Artists, Innovators, Musicians and Scientists; Writers is listed separately. AI is prohibited in Artists, Musicians and Scientists. Innovators allow disclosed AI use, but every essay/reflection/explanation must be written directly by the student without AI. English required except music with an English translation. Winning work may be showcased; ownership/future publication rights remain with the student. Bennington tuition awards require enrollment.

name: Sejong Writing Competition: Sijo (Pre-college Division)
value: Published 2026 pre-college prizes: $500 first, $400 second, $300 third, and $50 honorable mentions. Organizers reserve the right not to award prizes. Final 2027 awards are not published.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was February 28, 2026 (11:59 PM CT).
apply: Write one sijo (Korean poetic form) in English on any topic and submit it through the Sejong Cultural Society website without your name on the entry.
eligibility: Published 2026 pre-college division: U.S./Canadian residents age 18 or younger at the deadline, regardless of ethnic background. An 18-year-old already attending college must enter the adult division; younger students cannot enter adult division. Final 2027 criteria are not published.
notes: The essay category was discontinued beginning in 2026; sijo continues. Published rules require original work and disclosure of AI assistance; excessive reliance may disqualify. Organizers may publish any submitted work without compensation. This U.S./Canada pre-college contest is separate from the all-ages International Sijo Competition.

name: Federal Junior Duck Stamp Conservation and Design Contest
value: Published national awards: $1,000 first, $500 second, $200 third, and $200 for the conservation message winner. The 2025-26 brochure includes a free First Day of Issue trip for the national art winner and one parent/guardian. Final 2027 national award/travel terms are not posted. State prizes vary.
deadline: Enter through your state of legal residence, by its postmark deadline. Confirm the current date with your state coordinator. Published 2027 examples: Maryland February 1, 2027; Maine March 1, 2027. The complete 2027 state/national schedule is not confirmed on the national page.
apply: Mail original hand-illustrated 9 x 12 inch horizontal artwork, less than 1/4 inch thick, to your state coordinator, with a signed entry form attached to the back. Grades 7 to 12 must include the artistic reference form. Depict an eligible native North American duck, swan or goose; no traced/copied images, photography, computer-generated/printed art, lettering, signatures, borders, frames or mats. An original short conservation message is encouraged, not required. State Best of Show entries advance nationally. The detailed brochure still carries the 2025-26 label; confirm the current state forms.
eligibility: K-12 students at U.S./territory public, private, tribal or home schools; U.S. citizens abroad enter through their legal state of residence. National placement/monetary prizes require U.S. citizenship, resident-alien status or U.S. national status, with identity/residency documentation as requested. Foreign exchange students may be honored at state level but cannot advance as Best of Show. One entry per student; the preceding year's national first-place winner cannot enter.
notes: The national 2025-26 brochure grants FWS exclusive reproduction rights to the national winning design, promotional use of student names/art/photos without compensation, and a requirement for the winner to autograph stamps/products without charge. Artwork may tour and is not insured against loss/damage; keep a digital copy. Next-cycle national awards and updated detailed brochure are not published.

name: Brower Youth Awards
value: $3,000 cash prize, a co-produced short film about the recipient's work, and a leadership trip with flight, meals and lodging
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was March 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.
apply: Complete your own online application with a photograph; parents, teachers, friends and mentors cannot complete it for you. Semifinalists provide a support letter from someone familiar with their environmental work, excluding parents/guardians, and attend a video call. Complete 2027 forms are not published.
eligibility: Published 2026 rules: environmental change leaders ages 13 to 22 at the deadline, living in North America including Mexico, Canada and U.S. territories. Applicants must play a major leadership role in creating, organizing and implementing their effort. Final 2027 criteria are not published.
notes: The program generally favors leaders of ongoing group efforts. Standalone research/science-fair projects are excluded unless part of an ongoing environmental effort with a larger group; one-time events are generally excluded unless they produced measurable lasting impact with continuing leadership.

name: BMI Composer Awards (Student Composer Awards)
value: Individual award amounts are not specified. Special honors include the Ellen Taaffe Zwilich Prize for the most outstanding work and Carlos Surinach Prize for the youngest winner.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 cycle measured age as of February 15, 2026. Sign up on the BMI Foundation site for deadline notices.
apply: Submit one anonymously scored original classical composition and an audio rendering generated by music-engraving software. Only rendered/MIDI audio is accepted, rather than a live-performance recording; an additional sound file is allowed for electronics/non-notatable elements. A transposed or C-score is allowed. For another author's text provide permission or public-domain proof. No co-composed, previously awarded/recognized, or publisher/record-label contracted works; no identifying marks beyond title/composition. Do not enter the same work in another BMI Foundation award program. The full 2027 portal is not published.
eligibility: Published 2026 rules: under age 28 on February 15, 2026, and resident of the U.S./territories or citizen of a Western Hemisphere country. At most two prior BMI Composer Awards, excluding honorable mentions, to reapply. Exact 2027 age-reference date and criteria are not published.
notes: The program distributes a total $20,000 annual prize budget across winners, not $20,000 per winner. Winners are honored in New York each spring; score donations to the NYPL archive are voluntary. High-school entrants compete with older college/graduate composers.

provider: Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute
name: Ronald Reagan Debate Series (Great Communicator Debate Series)
value: Published historical national prizes include $10,000 first and $7,500 runner-up in 2023. Final 2027 individual scholarship amounts and award-use/payment terms are not published. Current 2027 rules provide national qualifiers a flight and hotel room for themselves and one chaperone.
deadline: 2026-27 regional events: Irvine November 14, 2026; Richmond February 20, 2027; Dallas March 6, 2027; Thousand Oaks March 13, 2027; Las Vegas/Springfield April 3, 2027; Shepherdstown/Redding April 10, 2027; Independence April 30 to May 1, 2027; New York May 1, 2027; Salt Lake City May 8, 2027; Honolulu May 22, 2027; online June 5, 2027. Registration closes before each event; check its official Tabroom invitation. Georgia/Arkansas dates and 2027 national championship date are not published.
apply: An adult coach/parent registers students through Tabroom; student-only teams are not allowed. Each institution provides at least one judge, plus another for every two students beyond two. Irvine/Richmond invitations state a nonrefundable $15 fee per debater with hardship help; entries stay waitlisted until judges and payment are entered. Complete the media release, with parent/guardian signature under 18. Compete in at most one geographic regional and/or the nationwide online regional; the current handbook advances one winner per region to nationals.
eligibility: Current handbook permits grades 9 to 12, excluding middle school students. Accredited high school, virtual school and homeschool participants are eligible; the Richmond invitation also allows mid-year graduates. An approved adult must supervise in-person students and be judging or immediately available online. Confirm any regional-specific eligibility in its invitation.
notes: 2027 regional topic concerns state/local versus federal responsibility for disaster preparedness and response. Use printed speech/research materials only; no laptops/tablets during rounds, phones for timing only. Each debater has two minutes optional prep time. The current page advertises a total $50,000 scholarship budget, not a per-student award.

provider: Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute

Covers education expenses charged through the student account, including tuition, fees, required books/supplies and on-campus room/board; generally excludes off-campus housing, transport, groceries, student loans and outside-account books.

The dated 2026 eligibility list requires 3.0/4.0 GPA or equivalent and full-time accredited four-year U.S. study, including homeschool and U.S. Armed Forces-base students abroad. name: Hispanic Heritage Youth Awards
value: One-time educational/community-service grant up to $4,000, depending on category. Gold, Silver and Bronze honors within categories, plus one National Youth Award recipient per category.
deadline: November 1, 2026 at 11:59:59 PM PST (application and document uploads)
apply: Submit the online application and one recommendation letter plus an official or unofficial school transcript by the same deadline. Complete four required essays up to 250 words each and one required community-service essay up to 400 words; an additional 250-word personal essay is optional. Multiple category applications are allowed; only one recommendation can be uploaded. Recommenders/schools can upload documents through the portal link, with no mail/email submission. Submitted category applications cannot be edited, but can be deleted/replaced before the deadline.
eligibility: High school/homeschool students graduating spring 2027, living in the U.S./territories, with at least 3.0 unweighted GPA on a 4.0 scale (or 7.5/10), entering an accredited higher education institution in 2027-28. FAQ also allows GED applicants under age 21. Current published eligibility does not state a Hispanic-heritage requirement. Virtual category ceremony attendance is mandatory; national recipients also attend the in-person ceremony.

Grants can support college education or a community-service effort. The deadline uses the sponsor's exact PST label; do not substitute a different zone.

name: Young American Creative Patriotic Art Contest (and 3-D Patriotic Art Contest)
value: 2026-27 national 2-D prizes: $15,000 first; $7,500 second; $4,500 third; $4,000 fourth; $1,500 fifth/sixth; $1,000 seventh-tenth; $750 eleventh; $500 twelfth-twenty-third. 3-D prizes: $2,500 first, $1,500 second, $1,000 third/fourth, $500 fifth. Paid directly to the chosen American college, university or vocational/technical school after verification; funds may be held for up to five years after high school graduation.
deadline: March 31, 2027: student entries to a participating sponsoring VFW Auxiliary. April 15, 2027: local/district winners to state judging. May 5, 2027: state first-place entries received at national headquarters. Students cannot enter directly at nationals.
apply: Submit original current-school-year art with separate contest form signed by student and parent/guardian, plus an artist statement up to 250 words. For 2-D submit paper/canvas art 8 by 10 inches minimum and 18 by 24 maximum including mat, one finished-art image, and no frame; canvas must be properly mounted/reinforced. For 3-D use raw materials, maximum 18 inches in any direction and five pounds, describe creation steps, and include at least three images from different angles. Referenced inspiration must be documented with a copy, source name and publication date. Local then state winners advance. Students may enter both contests with separate forms.
eligibility: Grades 9 to 12 by March 31, 2027 at U.S./territory schools or homeschool, or overseas dependents of U.S. military/civilian personnel. Citizenship is not required: lawful permanent residents or applicants whose permanent-residence application has not been denied and who intend to become citizens qualify. No foreign-exchange, age 20 or older, GED or adult-education students. Prior national winners cannot reenter the same contest; no VFW family relationship required.
notes: The current June 2026 rules supersede older prize amounts on the landing page/info sheet. Digital art, photography, weapons, 3-D printed art and jewelry are excluded; 2-D rules explicitly exclude AI art. Any flag must comply with the Federal Flag Code. Entry signatures grant permission for website/social-media publication and promotional use; artwork remains the student's property.

provider: National Society Daughters of the American Revolution
name: Dr. Aura-Lee A. and James Hobbs Pittenger American History Scholarship
value: $2,000 per year for up to four years, with annual transcript review and at least 3.25 GPA for renewal. Funds go directly to the institution for allowed educational expenses.
deadline: Portal opens November 1, 2026. Application and all materials due January 31, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. Hawaii Time.
apply: Apply through DAR Academic Works with a career-objectives personal statement up to 1,000 words, transcript (unofficial initially), one-page activities/awards/service/work resume, citizenship proof and two to four nonrelative recommendation letters written within the last year, signed and containing contact details. The applicant uploads every letter; recommenders cannot submit directly or through confidential third-party systems. All documents must be typed; conceal all photographs and Social Security numbers. A photograph or expired passport disqualifies. No generative AI or writing by others. Winners supply official transcripts and acceptance form. Homeschool applicants should check the conflicting grade ranges in the FAQ/checklist before uploading transcripts.
eligibility: Graduating high school students who are U.S. citizens and will pursue an undergraduate degree with at least 24 credit hours in American history and American government. A history major is not specifically required. U.S. citizens abroad may apply through a Units Overseas chapter.
notes: No DAR membership or chapter sponsor required. Only one DAR scholarship per award cycle. Funds cover institution-allowed tuition/fees, room/board, books and other educational expenses; unused funds are returned. Awards are issued in August while enrolled and cannot be deferred for a gap year. Military academies unable to accept restricted awards are ineligible.

name: Dr. Bart Kamen Memorial FIRST Scholarship
value: Up to four $10,000 initial grants, renewable for three more years (up to $40,000). Renewal requires continued full-time eligible study and satisfactory academic progress, annual biomedical/medical research, a scholarly paper and supervisor assessment, renewal letter, official transcript and W-9 by June 1. Funds are sent to selected applicants by August 31 after enrollment/tax-form verification.
deadline: Application opens annually but exact 2027 submission dates are unpublished and the official portal currently has no open calls. General later stages: enrollment by May 1; renewal research/letter/transcript by June 1; deferment request by July 1; disbursement by August 31. These recurring dates do not establish a 2027 application deadline.
apply: Complete the online Submittable application and supporting documents when open. An interview may be requested. Recipients must provide W-9 and verify admission/enrollment. The current portal has no open calls, so full initial application materials for 2027 cannot be read.
eligibility: Secondary-school seniors or graduates who have not begun full-time undergraduate study; at least one year on a FIRST LEGO League, Tech Challenge or Robotics Competition team. Apply to or be accepted by full-time biomedical engineering, premedical or another major with medical-school prerequisite coursework at a U.S. Title-IV-eligible institution or similarly accredited foreign institution. FIRST employees/officers, board/selection committee members and the specified close relatives are excluded. Citizenship is not explicitly stated; the required W-9 creates an unresolved tax-document question for non-U.S. applicants.
notes: Financial need may be considered but is not required. A biomedical engineering major is not mandatory if the programme permits premedical prerequisites with another major. Annual research is a renewal obligation. Deferment is discretionary, requires eligibility when deferred/paid, July 1 notice, and educational use of all funds; misuse can lead to cancellation/recoupment.
